overall: MARGINAL overall: Coron side and Panlaitan fine, west windy until about 1 PM, showers tonight
limiterDetail: The main limiter this morning is wind in the west: Ciron 15–20 kt and Nangalao 16–19 kt about 7 AM–noon, Cabunlawan and Decabaitot 14–18 kt and Barangonan 14–16.5 kt about 8–11 AM, Alava and Binudac 15–16 kt about 8–11 AM. It eases to 6–11 kt about 2–6 PM, then the west picks up again to 13–16 kt about 7–8 PM. Current is second: Barangonan is 1.0 kt now (easing to 0.5 by 8 AM), Tara and Turda build to 1.0–1.2 kt about 6–11 PM, and Decabaitot, Alava and Barangonan reach 0.9–1.2 kt again about 3–5 AM Sun. Rain is light by day, then showers about 9 PM–midnight (up to 3.4 mm/h at Coron, Culion and Galoc).

pagasa.detail: PAGASA: CLEAR. No gale, wind signal or heavy-rain warning for Calamian / MIMAROPA (latest entries are Davao Region gale advisories). The feed also carries a tropical cyclone alert for Typhoon Rosal (Champi) that doesn't name Palawan; worth a glance on the PAGASA site.

changed.title: ⚠️ What changed since yesterday afternoon
items: Tuesday 3 supply improved to NEAR NORMAL (was soft). Monday now looks calmer and dry (9.4 kt, gusts 15, was 12 kt with 1.9 mm), so boats go back out Monday and the soft run shrinks to Sunday and Monday arrivals. Wednesday 4 also firms to near normal (Tuesday 8.7 kt).

The catch: this morning's wind in the west is stronger than forecast, 16–20 kt about 7 AM–1 PM at Ciron, Nangalao, Cabunlawan, Decabaitot, Barangonan, Alava and Binudac (was 13–15 kt). Saturday is drier overall (3.9 mm regional, was 8.0), so Sunday 1 stays SLIGHTLY SOFT and today stays NEAR NORMAL. Sunday is still the wettest day (15.9 mm, was 14.1), so the Monday 2 dip stays. Grounds read 7 GOOD / 8 MARGINAL / 1 POOR / 0 VERY POOR (yesterday afternoon 5 GOOD / 11 MARGINAL / 0 POOR). PAGASA shows no warning for Palawan.

shortageRisk: Surge flag OFF (unchanged). The dashboard's shortage detector stays ELEVATED for Sat–Fri (guide only). Tightening risk is now two days, Sunday and Monday arrivals (was Sunday through Tuesday). Stock up from today's landings and lean on the Coron side, Panlaitan, Maglalambay and Galoc.
